accuracy.evidence: Every number is checked: 60 cm scarf = 3 straws of 20 cm = 12 clips of 5 cm; 24 cm ribbon = 6 units of 4 cm, 3 of 8 cm, 12 of 2 cm; 1 inch = 2.54 cm exactly (NIST), so 28 cm = 11.02 in, 18 cm = 7.09 in, 30 cm = 11.8 in (about 12) and 20 cm = 7.9 in (about 8). The lab ruler draws inch ticks at 2.54 cm spacing on the same scale as the cm ticks, so the book really ends at 11 and the pencil at 7. Foot counts (8 vs 5, 4 vs 7, 6 vs 9) always make the smaller count the longer foot.

misconceptions.evidence: Targets the slips documented for CCSS 2.MD.2 and Year 2 measurement: a bigger unit gives a bigger number (step 2 prediction, Kai's 8 feet prediction, challenge tag 'big'), the count stays the same whatever the unit ('The same: 3' option, tag 'same'), gaps and overlaps (robot saying 3, practice p4, mastery m6), starting the ruler at 1 (robot saying 4, challenge tag 'zero', p5, m8) and a number with no unit (challenge tag 'unit', m5).

lab_distinct.evidence: The lab is built on this topic's own mechanism, the inverse link between unit size and count: the same scarf is laid with two units, a unit's length is dragged until the ribbon takes 6, 3 and 12 of them, one ruler is read on its cm and inch sides, and two foot counts of one rug are compared. Lab shingle check passes the 30% limit against every other flagship; it differs from flaglenht (one non-standard unit), flagunits (choosing a unit per quantity) and flagconv (×10/×100/×1000 conversion).

lab_teaches.evidence: The learner discovers the rule before the text states it: laying 3 straws and then 12 clips along the same scarf shows the count rising while the scarf stays put; the drag scene makes them lengthen the unit to get fewer (3) and shorten it to get more (12); the ruler scene shows 28 cm and 11 in for one book; the foot scene asks them to reason backwards from counts to unit size. The done messages only confirm what they did.

predictions.evidence: Three locked predictions, each with a tempting wrong option the lab then disproves: 'Fewer clips' or 'The same: 3' before laying 12 clips; 'More inches' before the ruler shows 28 cm vs 11 in; 'Kai: 8 is more' before the rug shows Mum's 5 longer feet. The done message names the learner's own prediction and the right answer.

challenge_feedback.evidence: Six challenge questions; each wrong option carries a tag with its own message: 'big' (a longer unit fits fewer times), 'same' (same thing, different unit, different number), 'gap' and 'gapbig' (gaps make the count too small, not too big), 'zero' (from 1 to 9 is 8 cm), 'unit' (12 cm and 12 m are different). Wrong taps in the foot and robot scenes also name the slip, e.g. 'More feet fit, so Kai's foot is the shorter one.'

readability.evidence: Kid text uses short sentences and everyday objects (straw, paper clip, scarf, rug, feet) and passes the validator's kid readability limit; canvas labels are 2 to 8 words; the adult text names CCSS 2.MD.A.2 and Year 2 with the precise terms unit, length, end to end, centimetre, inch and ruler. The young class gives 56 px buttons and larger story text for ages 7 to 8.

no_filler.evidence: Every sentence teaches or checks: the key idea gives the rule, the 3-straw/12-clip example, the cm/inch example and the two habits (say the unit, start at 0); the filler gate passes; each practice and mastery item has its own context (plank, bench, desk, shelf, stick, path) with no repeated template text.

mobile.evidence: Checked iPhone 13 dark and desktop light screenshots of every step at rest, part-way through Show me and finished, plus a wrong challenge answer: the scarf with straws and clips fits the width with both rows and the dashed end lines visible; the ribbon count and 'Drag the handle' label stay on screen; the inch ruler shows 0 to 12 and the cm ruler 0 to 30 with readable numbers; the rug shows 8 and 5 distinct feet; robot sayings wrap onto two lines; buttons under the canvas wrap as large targets.

accessibility.evidence: Every canvas action has a labelled button twin: Lay a straw, Lay a paper clip, Shorter unit and Longer unit (1 cm steps reach 4, 8 and 2 cm from 5 cm), Slide left and Slide right (1 cm steps reach 0 from the 3 cm start), a button per person on the rug, and Right or Slip. Every change updates the canvas aria-label and c.say with the count or reading, and challenge feedback is a polite live region. The walk gate's axe run is clean in both themes on desktop and iPhone 13.
